blocks.text: Operators in Java are symbols that perform specific operations on one, two, or three operands and then return a result. Understanding these operators is crucial for writing efficient and correct Java code. This guide covers arithmetic, relational, and logical operators, their usage, and best practices.
Arithmetic operators perform mathematical operations on numeric operands.

items: The `/` operator performs integer division when both operands are integers.
The `%` operator works with floating-point numbers as well as integers.
Increment (`++`) and decrement (`--`) operators can be used as prefix or postfix.

blocks.text: Relational operators compare two values and return a boolean result.

items: These operators return `true` or `false`.
Be cautious when comparing floating-point numbers due to precision issues.
For object comparison, use `equals()` method instead of `==`.

blocks.text: Logical operators perform boolean logic operations.

rows: Bitwise AND (on booleans: logical AND, no short-circuit)
Bitwise OR (on booleans: logical OR, no short-circuit)

items: `&&` and `||` use short-circuit evaluation.
`&` and `|` evaluate both operands regardless of the first operand's value.
On boolean operands, the `^` operator returns `true` if the operands are different.
Operator precedence: Arithmetic > Relational > binary Logical (`&&`, `||`); the unary `!` binds tighter than all of them, so `!a == b` means `(!a) == b`.
Use parentheses to clarify complex expressions.
Be aware of integer overflow and underflow.
Short-circuit evaluation can improve performance and prevent errors.
Floating-point arithmetic may lead to precision errors.
Use `Math.floorDiv()` and `Math.floorMod()` for consistent behavior with negative numbers.
Consider using `java.util.concurrent.atomic` classes for thread-safe increment/decrement operations.

Use `Double.compare()` or `Float.compare()` when you need a consistent total order (they treat NaN as equal to itself and -0.0 as less than 0.0); they do not remove rounding error, so compare with a tolerance for that.

blocks.text: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

items: Using `==` to compare objects instead of `equals()`.
Integer division truncation: Use casting or floating-point division when needed.
Unintended side effects with increment/decrement operators in complex expressions.
Ignoring operator precedence, leading to unexpected results.

Use compound assignment operators (`+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`) for readability; they are not faster. Note that they contain an implicit narrowing cast: `byte b = 10; b += 300;` compiles and leaves `b == 54`.
Prefer `&&` and `||` over `&` and `|` for boolean operations to leverage short-circuit evaluation.
Use bitwise operators for performance-critical low-level operations.
Consider using `BigDecimal` for precise decimal calculations, especially in financial applications.
Division by zero: Use exception handling or check for zero before division.
Overflow/Underflow: Use `Math.addExact()`, `Math.multiplyExact()`, etc., for checked arithmetic.
NaN and Infinity: Be aware of special floating-point values and handle them appropriately.
Comparing NaN: Use `Double.isNaN()` or `Float.isNaN()` instead of relational operators.
